paper.title: Entailed Between the Lines: Incorporating Implication into NLI

source.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (repo LICENSE, added in commit 05c2e93 'changed License'); redistribution permitted with attribution under the same licence, so the frozen test file that scripts/prepare_inli.py writes is full-row JSONL and carries CC BY-SA 4.0

Resources/Few-shot LLM Results.xlsx.note: paper's 8-shot LLM outputs on the 4,000 test pairs (GPT-4, GPT-4o, Mistral-Large, Claude-3-Sonnet); used only to verify the metric definition, never shown to Jev

source.fields: unnamed row index, dataset (circa/ludwig/normbank/socialchem), premise, implied_entailment, explicit_entailment, neutral, contradiction (one row = one premise + its four hypotheses)

frozen.fields: id (inli-test-<row:04d>-<label>; never sent to Jev), group (premise row index), source_dataset, premise, hypothesis (verbatim), gold (release column name)

test_n_resolution: test.csv has 1,000 premise rows x 4 hypotheses = 4,000 pairs (README: 'Size of test dataset: 4,000'; train 8,000 / val 1,000 premises = 32,000 / 4,000 pairs; total 10,000 premises / 40,000 pairs = paper Section 1). Per-source pair totals over all splits equal paper Table 5 (LUDWIG 1,956; CIRCA 18,044; NORMBANK 10,000; SOCIALCHEM 10,000). The paper's released Table 6 LLM outputs contain exactly these 4,000 test pairs (3,999 exact matches; the last differs only by a trailing space in test.csv row 865 that the xlsx dropped). Test N = 4,000.
metric_verification: Table 6 'Implied Entailment' accuracy = accuracy on the 1,000 gold implied_entailment pairs (recall). Replaying the released few-shot outputs through inli.py score() gives GPT-4 0.753/0.645, GPT-4o 0.749/0.608, Mistral-Large 0.744/0.735 = Table 6 exactly. Claude-3-Sonnet's sheet has 1,022 'ERROR' responses; Table 6's 0.686 equals accuracy over the 2,978 non-error rows, so that row is not on the full test set.

english_verification.metadata: README and paper: premises/hypotheses generated in English by Gemini-Pro from English sources (LUDWIG, CIRCA, NormBank, Social Chemistry 101); names from the 2011 US Census.
english_verification.method: langid 1.1.6 on all 5,000 test texts (1,000 premises + 4,000 hypotheses), plus non-ASCII ratio > 5%; every flag inspected.
english_verification.result: 56 langid flags (af/es/sl/de/fr/...), all short English sentences with personal names (e.g. 'Alma desires a pay raise.', 'Heights frighten Stefanie.'); 0 non-ASCII flags (only 3 non-ASCII characters in the whole test set: 'canapé', 'après-ski', an en dash). No non-English rows; none dropped.

rows.93: implied_entailment == explicit_entailment ('Thad likes going to concerts.')
rows.477: implied_entailment == explicit_entailment ('This is Steven's first time living in the area.')

identical_hypothesis_text_under_two_labe.effect: kept as released (the paper scored them). Identical inputs get identical Jev answers, so at most one pair of each is correct: accuracy ceiling 3,997/4,000 = 0.99925

deviations: Zero-shot: the paper's LLM baselines used an 8-shot prompt (App. E.3, examples from train). Jev gets the E.3 instructions and label definitions without examples, plus the paper's Section 2 definitions of explicit/implied entailment.
